column1: > Duplicate-name disambiguation, session of 13 Aug 2026. Built on top of theme KK (batch 7).
> WHY: tjjm-gym-websites* and tjjm-gym-addresses match on NAME ALONE, corpus-wide. 12 names
> were carried by two or more LIVE records, so any override written for one would hit them all.
> Two pairs were same-name-SAME-REGION, where a single suppression deletes both records while
> the counts still reconcile. This blocks the repointing pass, which is bulk override work.
> METHOD: `n` cannot be rewritten in the legacy blob, so every rename is suppress-plus-add.
> Each renamed record is re-added to tjjm-gyms-data-45 with its stored w and a preserved.
> ⚠️ SAME-REGION PAIRS: suppression matches by name WITHIN a region, so one entry kills both
> copies. Those pairs must have BOTH copies renamed - you cannot rename just one. This makes
> two suppression entries match two records each, so suppressed NAMES (13) and suppressed
> RECORDS (15) diverge. The invariant is "stored - suppressed RECORDS == published".
> w and a are the values that render today. No website override exists for any of these 16
> names, so rendered w equals stored w. The only address override is Infinite Jiu-Jitsu, whose
> Phoenix record has NO stored `a` - that address is carried into the new record directly and
> the now-orphaned override entry is removed from tjjm-gym-addresses.
> kind: SAME-REGION = both copies renamed under one suppression entry
>       CROSS-REGION = one copy renamed, the other keeps the name
